title: Not ready yet
setting: Saturday evening at Kenta and Sora's flat. Yuki has come to pick Kenta up for dinner at Mai's. He promised to bring homemade gyoza, and they aren't done yet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kenta, junbi dekita? sorosoro deru yo.
lines.ja: ケンタ、準備できた？そろそろ出るよ。
lines.kana: けんた、じゅんびできた？そろそろでるよ。
lines.english: Kenta, are you ready? We need to head out soon.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: gomen, mou chotto. gyouza ga mada na n da.
lines.ja: ごめん、もうちょっと。餃子がまだなんだ。
lines.kana: ごめん、もうちょっと。ぎょうざがまだなんだ。
lines.english: Sorry, nearly there. The gyoza aren't done yet.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, mada tsukutteru no? gyouza tte, jikan kakaru yo ne?
lines.ja: え、まだ作ってるの？餃子って、時間かかるよね？
lines.kana: え、まだつくってるの？ぎょうざって、じかんかかるよね？
lines.english: What, you're still making them? Gyoza take ages, don't they?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jikan mo da kedo, tsutsumu no ga tema kakaru n da yo.
lines.ja: 時間もだけど、包むのが手間かかるんだよ。
lines.kana: じかんもだけど、つつむのがてまかかるんだよ。
lines.english: Time, sure, but it's the wrapping that's such a fiddly job.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.ja: あとどれぐらいかかる？
lines.kana: あとどれぐらいかかる？
lines.english: How much longer will it take?

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.kana: にじゅっぷんぐらいかな。

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: nijuppun mo? mai no uchi made ichijikan kakaru n da yo. densha ni maniawanai yo.
lines.ja: 二十分も？マイの家まで一時間かかるんだよ。電車に間に合わないよ。
lines.kana: にじゅっぷんも？まいのうちまでいちじかんかかるんだよ。でんしゃにまにあわないよ。
lines.english: Twenty whole minutes? It takes an hour to get to Mai's. We'll miss our train.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: jaa, tetsudatte! futari nara hayai yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、手伝って！二人なら早いよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、てつだって！ふたりならはやいよ。
lines.english: Then give me a hand! It'll go quicker with two of us.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: mou! tema kakaru no, nigate na n da kedo.
lines.ja: もう！手間かかるの、苦手なんだけど。
lines.kana: もう！てまかかるの、にがてなんだけど。
lines.english: Ugh! I'm hopeless at fiddly stuff.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.ja: 大丈夫。見て、こうやって、こう。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。みて、こうやって、こう。
lines.english: You'll be fine. Watch: like this, then this.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: e, dekinai! kore, honto ni tema kakaru ne.
lines.ja: え、できない！これ、ほんとに手間かかるね。
lines.kana: え、できない！これ、ほんとにてまかかるね。
lines.english: What? I can't do it! These really are a lot of work.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: boku mo kyonen no imagoro wa, ikko ni gofun mo kakatteta yo.
lines.ja: 僕も去年の今ごろは、一個に五分もかかってたよ。
lines.kana: ぼくもきょねんのいまごろは、いっこにごふんもかかってたよ。
lines.english: This time last year, I was taking five whole minutes per gyoza too.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: kyonen no imagoro? e, mou ichinen tatta n da.
lines.ja: 去年の今ごろ？え、もう一年経ったんだ。
lines.kana: きょねんのいまごろ？え、もういちねんたったんだ。
lines.english: This time last year? Wow, so it's been a year already.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: un. ichinen kakatte, yatto jouzu ni natta n da yo.
lines.ja: うん。一年かかって、やっと上手になったんだよ。
lines.kana: うん。いちねんかかって、やっとじょうずになったんだよ。
lines.english: Yeah. It took me a year to finally get good at it.

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: sokka. jikan tatsu no hayai ne.
lines.ja: そっか。時間経つの早いね。
lines.kana: そっか。じかんたつのはやいね。

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: yatto junbi dekita! a, mou sanjuppun tatteru. gomen!
lines.ja: やっと準備できた！あ、もう三十分経ってる。ごめん！
lines.kana: やっとじゅんびできた！あ、もうさんじゅっぷんたってる。ごめん！
lines.english: Ready at last! Oh, it's been thirty minutes already. Sorry!

lines.speaker: yuki
lines.romaji: daijoubu. ima mai kara renraku kita yo. mai mo mada junbi dekitenai tte.
lines.ja: 大丈夫。今マイから連絡来たよ。マイもまだ準備できてないって。
lines.kana: だいじょうぶ。いままいかられんらくきたよ。まいもまだじゅんびできてないって。
lines.english: It's fine. Mai just messaged. She says she isn't ready yet either.

lines.speaker: kenta
lines.romaji: nan da. jaa, mou chotto tsukureru ne.
lines.ja: なんだ。じゃあ、もうちょっと作れるね。
lines.kana: なんだ。じゃあ、もうちょっとつくれるね。
lines.english: Oh, is that all? Then I can make a few more.

choices.english: Kenta was ready on time, but they missed their train because Yuki took so long wrapping gyoza.
The gyoza took so long that Kenta called off the dinner, and Yuki went to Mai's on her own.
Kenta wasn't ready because the gyoza weren't done. Yuki helped, it ran half an hour over, and then Mai messaged that she wasn't ready either.

questions.explanation: Lines 1-2: Kenta isn't ready because the gyoza aren't done (gyouza ga mada na n da). Line 7: Yuki worries they'll miss the train. Lines 8-11: Kenta gets her to help wrap them. Line 16: he's finally ready, but thirty minutes have gone by (mou sanjuppun tatteru). Line 17: Mai has messaged that she isn't ready yet either (mai mo mada junbi dekitenai tte), so there's no rush, and in line 18 Kenta decides he can make a few more. A is wrong: Kenta wasn't ready (line 2), and nobody says they missed the train. B is wrong: nobody calls anything off; Yuki stays and helps, and Mai's message just means there's time to spare.

questions.english: When Yuki arrives at Kenta's flat, what does she ask him?
questions.ja: ユキさんは、ケンタさんに何と聞きましたか？
questions.kana: ゆきさんは、けんたさんになんとききましたか？
questions.romaji: yuki-san wa, kenta-san ni nan to kikimashita ka?

choices.english: Kenta, are you going to get ready?

questions.explanation: Line 1: kenta, junbi dekita? Japanese asks whether getting ready is done, so the question is in the past: dekita? = are you ready (yet)? Kenta answers in the same frame in line 16 (yatto junbi dekita!), and Mai's message in line 17 is mai mo mada junbi dekitenai (she isn't ready yet either). A copies English 'are you ready?' into the present: junbi dekiru? asks whether he is able to get ready. C, junbi suru?, asks whether he's going to start getting ready: junbi suru is doing the preparing, junbi ga dekiru is being done with it.

questions.english: Kenta asks you how long it takes to get from your place to his: "uchi kara koko made, dore gurai?" It's about thirty minutes by train. Tell him.
questions.ja: 家からここまで、どれぐらい？
questions.kana: うちからここまで、どれぐらい？
questions.romaji: uchi kara koko made, dore gurai?
questions.answer: Give the time with kakaru: densha de sanjuppun gurai kakaru yo.

modelAnswers.romaji: densha de sanjuppun gurai kakaru yo.
modelAnswers.ja: 電車で三十分ぐらいかかるよ。

modelAnswers.romaji: kekkou jikan kakaru yo. densha de sanjuppun gurai.
modelAnswers.ja: けっこう時間かかるよ。電車で三十分ぐらい。
modelAnswers.english: It takes a while. About thirty minutes by train.

questions.explanation: How long something takes is kakaru, with the amount where jikan would go: Yuki's mai no uchi made ichijikan kakaru (line 7) and ato dore gurai kakaru? (line 5), Kenta's ikko ni gofun mo kakatteta (line 12). On its own, jikan kakaru means 'it takes a while' (line 3), as in the second model answer. Don't reach for toru, English 'take': jikan o toru means making time for someone. And not tatsu: sanjuppun tatta would mean thirty minutes have gone by (line 16).

questions.english: When the gyoza are finally done, Kenta says "a, mou sanjuppun tatteru. gomen!" What does he mean?
questions.ja: 「もう三十分経ってる」は、どういう意味ですか？
questions.kana: 「もうさんじゅっぷんたってる」は、どういういみですか？
questions.romaji: mou sanjuppun tatteru wa, dou iu imi desu ka?

choices.english: Thirty minutes have already gone by while they were making the gyoza.
The gyoza will take another thirty minutes.
It takes thirty minutes to get to Mai's place.

questions.explanation: Line 16: tatsu is time going by, so mou sanjuppun tatteru = it's already been thirty minutes (in line 6 he guessed about twenty). B would be ato sanjuppun kakaru: kakaru is how long a job still takes, as in Yuki's ato dore gurai kakaru? (line 5), and the gyoza are already done. C mixes in the trip: Yuki said it takes an hour to get to Mai's, with kakaru (line 7: ichijikan kakaru). The same pair comes up in lines 13-14: mou ichinen tatta (a year has gone by) against ichinen kakatte (it took a year).

questions.english: Yuki, still fighting with a gyoza, asks you: "ne, gyouza tsukutta koto aru? dou datta?" You have made them, and it was a lot of fiddly work. Tell her.
questions.ja: ね、餃子作ったことある？どうだった？
questions.kana: ね、ぎょうざつくったことある？どうだった？
questions.romaji: ne, gyouza tsukutta koto aru? dou datta?
questions.answer: Say you have, and that it was fiddly work, with tema and kakaru: aru yo. demo, kekkou tema kakatta.

modelAnswers.romaji: aru yo. demo, kekkou tema kakatta.
modelAnswers.ja: あるよ。でも、けっこう手間かかった。
modelAnswers.english: I have. It was quite a lot of work, though.

modelAnswers.romaji: un, aru. tsutsumu no ga metcha tema kakaru yo ne.
modelAnswers.ja: うん、ある。包むのがめっちゃ手間かかるよね。
modelAnswers.english: Yeah, I have. Wrapping them is such a hassle, right?

questions.explanation: A fiddly, slow chore like wrapping gyoza is tema ga kakaru, with the same kakaru as jikan ga kakaru: Kenta in line 4 (tsutsumu no ga tema kakaru n da yo), Yuki in lines 9 and 11. English 'it takes a lot of effort' points to doryoku, but doryoku is effort as in trying hard (doryoku shita = I worked hard at it), not a chore being a hassle. jikan kakatta would only say it took a long time; tema is the fiddliness, which Kenta sets apart from time in line 4 (jikan mo da kedo...).
